lines: Solid trip, solid return. Foundations matter.
We left, returned, and nothing load-bearing failed. I'll take that.
Home is still standing, and so am I. That's a proper finish.
My workshop door has never looked so welcoming.
The road was rough, but you never pushed the group past its strength.
You waited when I needed rest. I noticed.
We came back with our supplies and all our names accounted for.
I trusted your route, and this time the route earned it.
The village bell sounded better than music on the last mile.
Nothing followed us home. I checked the road twice.
You chose the careful path when the short one looked unsafe.
I expected trouble. I did not expect you to handle it so calmly.
My boots need work, but the rest of me is sound.
We learned each other's pace before it became a problem.
I can complain about the hills now because none of them kept us.
Thank you for treating my safety like part of the plan.
The journey gave me stories without giving me scars.
I would travel with you again after my feet recover.
We left as strangers. I do not think we came back that way.
Safe, home, and tired is enough for tonight.
I came back chipped. A wall can take that. A person should not have to.
I made it home with damage that no chisel can smooth.
There are cracks in me that the road had no right to make.
I trusted you to keep the danger farther away than that.
Every step home reminded me where the plan broke.
My shoulder needs a bandage before we discuss another journey.
We should have turned back when I first asked to slow down.
I am grateful you did not leave me there.
Do not call the trip a success while I am still bleeding from it.
The supplies arrived in better condition than I did.
You carried my pack after I was hit. I will give you that.
I needed cover beside me, not ten steps ahead.
The cut will close. My questions about your judgment will take longer.
I kept walking because stopping out there felt worse.
Next time, listen before pride chooses the dangerous path.
I am home because you helped and hurt because the plan failed.
Let me sit down before you ask what I learned.
I will not travel again until these bruises fade.
Surviving does not make every choice along the way sound.
Bring me water now. We can argue after the room stops moving.
You cracked something load-bearing between us.
A careless blow can split more than stone.
Trust was holding weight. Then you struck it.
Do not call that blow a mistake. You chose where it landed.
I was far from every safe wall because I believed you.
The wound will close before the trust does.
You knew I would stay close. That is what makes it worse.
I made it home despite you, not because of you.
No repair begins by pretending the break never happened.
Do not ask me to make your apology easier.
I trusted your directions and your promise. Never again.
Keep away from my workshop until I decide what comes next.
The village will hear what happened from me.
You turned every kind moment on that road into a question.
I would rather walk alone than follow you again.
The bruise is simple. The reason behind it is not.
You were supposed to be the person I did not have to fear.
Leave me alone. You have guided me far enough.
Trust is not mortar. I cannot spread more over the crack.
If you want forgiveness, start by telling the truth to everyone.
No foundation under a boat, yet somehow it held. I respect the craft.
A boat has no proper base, but I can't argue with arriving alive.
The water carried us better than I expected. I still prefer roads.
We arrived wet, tired, and safe enough.
The hull leaked less than I feared and more than I liked.
I kept my tools dry while you handled the oars.
Our landing was rough, but at least it was on the right bank.
The river shortened the journey and lengthened my list of worries.
You found a calm channel when I could not see one.
I owe that little boat an apology for doubting every plank.
Next time, let me wrap the mortar before we push off.
I can still feel the dock moving under my feet.
We nearly lost an oar, then found a quieter way around the rocks.
The village roofs looked good from the water, especially as they got closer.
You handled the rough stretch better than I expected.
I would take that crossing again after someone checks the seams.
Nothing fell overboard, though my patience came close.
I spent the last mile planning my first step onto land.
The boat is empty, the gear is here, and the river can continue without us.
Home by water still counts as home.
